learn.title: Angles that work together
learn.body: Angles often come in pairs with a fixed relationship. Knowing the relationship lets you find an angle without measuring it. This is the first real tool of geometry.

learn.title: Complementary and supplementary
learn.body: Two angles are complementary if their measures add to $90^\circ$. They are supplementary if they add to $180^\circ$. Two angles that sit side by side on a straight line form a linear pair, and a linear pair is always supplementary.

learn.title: Vertical angles
learn.body: When two lines cross, they make four angles. The angles directly opposite each other are vertical angles, and they are always equal. If one is $70^\circ$, the opposite one is $70^\circ$ and the other two are each $110^\circ$.

learn.title: Angles with algebra
learn.body: Two angles with measures $x$ and $2x+30$ are supplementary. Find both.
Always check the sum. Here $50+130=180$, so the answer fits the rule.

questions.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is $70^\circ$. What is the angle next to it, sharing a side?
questions.explanation: Neighbouring angles at a crossing form a linear pair, so they add to $180^\circ$: $180-70=110$.
Opposite angles at a crossing are equal. Next-door angles are the supplementary ones.

questions.prompt: Two complementary angles measure $x$ and $2x$. Find $x$.
Angles of $x$ and $x+40$ are supplementary. What is $x$?
questions.explanation: $2x+40=180$ gives $2x=140$, so $x=70$. The angles are $70^\circ$ and $110^\circ$.
